data.title: The US consumer may be hitting a wall. A look at eight indicators
data.description:
The old addage is: Never underestimate the spending power of the US consumer.

That stance has been a remarkably good one for traders. Time after time, Americans have dug into their pockets and kept the economy churning.

data.title: Fed's Daly: In all likelihood, we need to raise rates
data.description:
• Hard to say policy is restrictive enough
  • In all likelihood, we will need to raise rates
  • A myriad of things are pushing up inflation, which makes it concerning
  • Bias is that rates need to go up

Every single Fed official speaking lately says that rates need to go up, and yet seemingly none of them supported a rate hike two weeks ago. It's baffling.

data.title: Earnings week ahead: Nvidia without Jensen, Anthropic’s IPO, and the consumer meets a hiking Fed
data.description:
Earnings season is supposed to be over. Instead, next week might be the most important of the quarter for the macro view.

Nvidia reports days after losing its founder. Anthropic prices what could be the largest equity deal ever. And every major US retailer reports into a rate-hike cycle. October CPI came in hot at 0.4% headline and 0.3% core, a December hike is fully priced with a 12% chance of 50 bps, 10-year yields sit at 5.13% and Brent is above $98.

data.title: Fed's Collins: I would think some additional policy tightening is warranted soon
data.description:
• Possible Fed may ahve to raise more than expected
  • Best care scenario is 'careful adjustment' of mon pol
  • Labor market appears on solid footing
  • The future direction of mon pol is clear
  • Recent inflation data less promising than I hope
  • Inflation is too high and appears to be broadening

I don't see any way the Fed doesn't hike in December and now the market sees a 75% chance of back-to-back hikes. Today, Bank of America forecast back-to-back to back hikes in Dec, Jan and March.

data.title: Goldman Sachs: We can explain almost the entire US inflation overshoot by tariffs and the war in Iran
data.description:
Goldman Sachs is out with a chart that says the US inflation problem is almost entirely two things: tariffs and the Iran energy shock. Take those out and inflation is basically at target.

The latest hard data is ugly. September PCE was 3.6% y/y on headline and 3.1% on core, with gasoline and other energy goods up 9.2% in the month alone. Goldman sees headline peaking just shy of 3.9% right about now and core topping out near 3.3%.

data.title: Xlence prepares for Anthropic’s anticipated IPO
data.description:
Anthropic, the company behind the Claude family of AI models, is preparing for a potential initial public offering (IPO). With an expected valuation of $2 trillion and a planned Nasdaq ticker of ANTH, its market debut could become a major event for the technology sector.

Known for its work in developing advanced AI models, Anthropic has attracted attention from businesses and investors as interest in artificial intelligence continues to grow.

data.title: Trading Sphere eyes Anthropic IPO with plans for day-one CFD trading
data.description: Traders will be able to access Anthropic share CFDs opportunities from day one of its anticipated market debut.

data.title: Fed's Goolsbee: We're not on the way to 2% inflation and we have to deal with that
data.description:
• Inflation has spread into categories where prices not driven by energy
  • The jobs market looks stable, if not tightening a bit
  • Rates will eventually go well-below today
  • We have had signs of trouble for several months in a row now
  • Inflation is rising and proving far more persistent than expected when it was just a matter of supply shocks
  • The Fed "definitely has work to do" to maintain its credibility
  • Services inflation and rising health care costs don't feel like they will change quickly
  • Even if the price of oil goes down rapidly, refining capacity is still very problematic
  • My feeling is that right now we're not on the way to 2% and we have to deal with that
  • Demand-overheating inflation shocks are extremely hard to get rid of

data.title: US October PPI +6.5% vs +6.6% expected
data.description:
• Prior was 6.3%
  • PPI final demand m/m +0.3% vs +0.4  expected
  • Prior m/m +1.3%
  • Ex-food and energy y/y +5.0% vs +5.0%  expected
  • Prior ex-food and energy 5.0% y/y
  • Ex-food and energy m/m +0.3% vs +0.3% expected
  • Prior ex-food and energy +0.7% m/m
  • Ex-food, energy and trade y/y +4.9% vs +5.0% prior
  • Ex-food, energy and trade m/m +0.5% vs +0.5% prior

The market is increasingly concerned about rising inflation but this is a slight relief, with some bids in bonds afterwards and modest USD selling. We will hear from the Fed's Goolsbee on CNBC momentarily and he recently called inflation "borderline alarming". Ahead of the data, the market was pricing in 28.5 bps of hikes for December, which is a bit over a 10% chance of a 50 bps move, with 86 bps in hikes priced in over the coming year.

data.title: Nasdaq's suckers' rally is approaching a key resistance amid hawkish Fed bets, US-Iran tensions
data.description:
The Nasdaq recovered all the losses from last Thursday’s sharp selloff amid a dip-buying wave and reassessment of AI-related risks.

Nevertheless, this recovery looks increasingly like a “suckers’ rally” amid more hawkish Fed bets, higher Treasury yields and a stronger US dollar.

data.title: Solana remains under pressure amid hawkish Fed bets and renewed US-Iran tensions. What's next?
data.description:
Solana extended the selloff as Trump's remarks on Iran triggered another wave of risk-off flows across crypto markets. The US dollar and Treasury yields jumped after Trump stated that the US doesn’t need a deal with Iran, fuelling inflation concerns and expectations of additional rate hikes.

This continues to create a challenging environment for Solana amid tightening financial conditions and growth concerns.

data.title: Wall Street steadies despite Nvidia drama but dip buyers are still walking a tight rope
data.description:
Just about everyone seems to be kicking and screaming about how Jensen Huang is tearing down the whole AI boom. And if you listen to the social media echo chamber, you might think tech stocks have already crashed into oblivion. Well, here's a little reality check. As of the close yesterday, the Nasdaq is keeping within 10% from its record highs in early October and is still up by 9% this year.

So, let's take a step back and put the funeral arrangements on hold for now, shall we?

data.title: Crude oil jumps as escalation risks increase after Trump says the US doesn't need Iran deal
data.description:
Crude oil jumped yesterday after Trump stated on Truth Social that the US does not need a deal with Iran, fuelling escalation concerns.

Trump warned that the US would not hesitate to take further military action if current measures fail to achieve objectives, while CENTCOM is implementing the naval blockade and working to restore commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

data.title: Eurozone Q3 GDP unchanged in second estimate as uneven growth clouds the outlook
data.description:
• Eurozone Q3 GDP second estimate +0.4% vs +0.4% q/q prelim
  • Prior +0.6%
  • Eurozone Q3 GDP second estimate +1.3% vs +1.3% y/y prelim
  • Prior +1.2%

There are no changes to the initial estimates as the euro area economy holds up in Q3. As a reminder, expectations were for a growth of just 0.2% on the quarter on the initial report. So, the second estimate here mainly reaffirms the beat we saw from two weeks back.

data.title: The macro backdrop remains negative for Ethereum as Trump's Iran remarks fuel renewed risk aversion
data.description:
Ethereum extended the selloff after Trump stated on Truth Social that the US doesn’t need a deal with Iran, triggering another wave of risk-off flows across markets.

The US dollar and Treasury yields jumped following his remarks on increased inflation concerns and expectations of additional rate hikes.

data.title: European stock market open: Stocks ease slightly as the rally takes a breather
data.description:
Well, it looks like the European stock market party is finally running out of a little steam. The music hasn't completely stopped but investors are certainly turning down the volume as we head into the final trading day of the week.

The opening mood is erring more on the cautious side after the more subdued showing in Wall Street overnight. The declines aren't anything that jumps out of the page and after the strong gains earlier this week, perhaps a little check back was overdue. Here's how things are looking at the open:

data.title: Higher real yields and stronger US dollar weigh on gold as Trump puts Iran deal in jeopardy
data.description:
Gold extended the losses yesterday after Trump stated on Truth Social that the US does not need a deal with Iran and directed Vice President Vance to focus on domestic matters.

The US dollar and Treasury yields jumped following his remarks, while oil prices extended the gains, fuelling inflation concerns and expectations of additional rate hikes.
